subject: Having trouble calculating true density of my data!!!

messages.author: eceaf8d32dda4993
messages.subject: Having trouble calculating true density of my data!!!
parts:
Hi everyone, I am trying to calculate true density for my provided data but everytime I try to run the program in R I get a CoveredArea that is 3x the size of my intended area.

My code is as follows:

library(mrds)
library(Distance)
Birdhouse<-read.csv("RCode Birds4.csv")
attach(Birdhouse)
head(Birdhouse)
str(Birdhouse)
b.f <- checkdata(Birdhouse)
bird <- b.f$data
region <- b.f$region.table
sample <- b.f$sample.table
obs <- b.f$obs.table
head(b.f)
bf <- ds(bird, truncation = list(left=20, right=320), transect = "point", formula=~individuals, key= c("hn"), adjustment = c("cos"), dht.group = FALSE
          , region.table = region, sample.table = sample, obs.table = obs,convert.units = 1, method = "nlminb", quiet = FALSE, debug.level = 0,
         initial.values = NULL)
summary(bf)

A example of my data is as follows:
object   Region.Label   Area Effort Sample.Label distance individuals      detected observer
1      1    House 1.1     7850      1        SS.20          20             8                   1         1
2      2    House 1.2     7850      1        SS.120       120             5                   1         1
3      3    House 1.3     7850      1        SS.220       220             3                   1         1
4      4    House 1.4     7850      1         SS.320      320             5                   1         1
5      5    House 2.1     7850      1         SS.20         20              9                   1         1
6      6    House 2.2     7850      1        SS.120       120             5                   1         1

My data was collected using sampling stations at 4 distances away from a different buildings (20, 120, 220, 320 meters). I got number of individuals of all the various birds (this data groups them regardless of species) and I am trying to calculate true density due to the fact with a survey distance of 50 meters per plot, I might have missed individuals while surveying. 

I was wondering if anyone has run into a similar problem or know how I might fix either the code or my data to achieve the goals I have set in place?

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Having trouble calculating true density of my data!!!
parts:
Eric

Several unusual things about your code, data, and study description.  Perhaps one (or several) of these anomalies might be causing your difficulties.  Here are my observations:

- if you data are arranged as you show, you should not need to call checkdata() and use obs, region and sample.  ds() should do all those things for you.

- Distance thinks of 'region' as strata.  The snippet of data you show has the value of region (or strata) changing for each of the 6 records you show.  That seems improbable; you should have multiple transects per strata with multiple (hopefully) detections per transect.  I suspect you are not organising your data properly.

- Your point counts have 3 distance bins from what you describe.  Because of this you can only fit very simple models-a half-normal with a single parameter, if you want to be able to test goodness-of-fit.  (see my answer on this subject to the list on 5 October 2016)

- I cannot reconcile your statement about "50 metres per plot" with your strata area or distance bins

- Left truncation of point transect data is not a good idea.

- The statement "sampling stations at 4 distances away from a different buildings" has me confused.  Were you making observations from the building (not the best idea) or were you standing at the 4 distances you describe (20, 120, 220, 320)?  If the latter, then these are not the distance bins you should use in your analysis.

parts:
Thank you for the help,

I'll try your recommendations as soon as possible but to answer your questions I thought I might clarify my methods a little bit. 

When I was doing my surveys instead of doing a transect line I did points surveys at increasing increments away from the house. These survey points were at 20 meters away from the house, 120, etc. Once I got to the distance I wanted away from the house (20 meters for example) I would wait a few minutes and then start a 5 minute survey in which I would count any birds that landed within 50 meters from where I was standing. Once the 5 minutes were up I would walk to the next survey point and continue with the survey. I did not count any that I saw while walking to each point.

I hope this clarifies a few things.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Having trouble calculating true density of my data!!!
parts:
Eric

I don't really think you are applying distance sampling in what you describe.  In reality you weren't measuring distance between you and the detected birds, but just any bird that landed while you were standing at these specified distances from a building.

Have a read through fundamental papers such as this from the Encyclopedia of Environmetrics

http://distancesampling.org/downloads/dist_encyc_env.pdf
